title: Claude Code: Dynamic Workflows & Scheduled Deployments
content:
## Overview

In mid-2026 Anthropic shipped a set of Claude Code features that substantially expand what autonomous agents can do: **dynamic multi-agent workflows** (generally available June 2026), **scheduled deployments**, **Dreaming**, **Outcomes**, and enhanced multiagent orchestration. Together they move Claude Code from an interactive tool into a platform for persistent, self-improving agentic systems.

---

## Dynamic Workflows

Dynamic workflows allow a single Claude Code session to spawn **hundreds of parallel subagents**, each working concurrently on different parts of a task. Previously, multi-agent orchestration required manual session management; dynamic workflows handle concurrency, result merging, and context handoffs automatically.

**When to use:**
- Large-scale refactors spanning many files
- Parallel test generation across a codebase
- Multi-repository analysis where each repo is a subagent's domain
- Simultaneous research and implementation tasks

The lead agent defines the work decomposition; each subagent operates on a shared filesystem and reports results back to the coordinator.

---

## Scheduled Deployments

Scheduled deployments give an agent a **cron schedule**. Each time the schedule fires, the agent starts a fresh session, completes its task, commits any changes, and exits — with no external scheduler to build or host.

```
Schedule: every day at 06:00 UTC
Prompt: Review all open PRs for merge conflicts and CI failures.
        Post a summary comment on any PR that needs attention.
Repo: my-org/my-repo
Model: claude-sonnet-4-6
```

Configuration is done in the Claude Code web interface (claude.ai/code): attach repos, set environment variables, connect to MCP servers, and choose a model — then the agent runs on schedule even when your computer is off.

**Common use cases:**
- Morning PR triage
- Nightly CI failure summaries
- Weekly dependency audits
- Doc synchronization after merges

---

## Dreaming

**Dreaming** is a scheduled background process that runs after regular agent sessions to improve future performance:

1. Reviews logs from past sessions
2. Surfaces recurring patterns (common mistakes, repeated workflows, team conventions)
3. Curates those patterns into agent memory

Over time, an agent with Dreaming enabled builds up a more accurate model of how your team works — preferred file structures, naming conventions, common debugging approaches — without requiring explicit configuration. Dreaming runs on a separate schedule from task deployments and does not produce code changes itself.

---

## Multiagent Orchestration

The enhanced orchestration model uses a **lead agent + specialist subagents** structure:

- **Lead agent:** Maintains the high-level goal, decomposes work, assigns subtasks, and merges results. Runs on a capable model (Sonnet or Opus/Fable).
- **Specialist subagents:** Each has its own model selection, system prompt, and tool set. Can be optimized for their domain — a fast Haiku model for file search, a capable Sonnet for code generation.
- **Shared filesystem:** Subagents coordinate through a shared workspace rather than passing large blobs of context between them, reducing token overhead.

This pattern scales to tasks that would overflow a single context window — the lead agent tracks the big picture while subagents handle local concerns.

---

## Outcomes

**Outcomes** lets you define a rubric for what a good agent result looks like, then automatically evaluates each run against it:

1. Developer defines the rubric (e.g., "all tests pass", "no regressions in benchmark scores", "PR description includes a test plan")
2. A separate grader model evaluates the agent's output against the rubric
3. If the output doesn't meet the bar, the agent is sent back to revise
4. Loop continues until the rubric is satisfied or a retry limit is hit

Outcomes turns single-shot tasks into self-correcting loops without requiring you to manually review each run.

---

## Putting It Together

A typical production setup combining these features:

```
Scheduled deployment (daily):
  Lead agent (Sonnet 4.6): Identify failing tests in CI
    → Subagent 1 (Haiku): Fetch CI logs
    → Subagent 2 (Sonnet): Diagnose root causes
    → Subagent 3 (Sonnet): Write fixes
  Outcomes rubric: "All tests pass after applying changes"
  Dreaming: Runs nightly to learn from session logs
```

The lead agent runs on schedule, coordinates specialist subagents, evaluates results against the Outcomes rubric, and over time Dreaming improves how well the system understands your codebase and test patterns.

---

## Availability

- **Dynamic workflows:** Generally available as of June 2026 (announced at the Code with Claude Tokyo event, June 10, 2026)
- **Scheduled deployments:** Public beta as of June 2026 via Claude Managed Agents
- **Dreaming:** Available to teams using Claude Managed Agents
- **Outcomes:** Available in Claude Code for teams
- All features require a Claude team or enterprise plan
